text.p: Micron Technology Inc Monday said three company executives were giving up their seats on the board of directors.
In statement issued late Monday, the semiconductor company said Ed Heitzeberg, Tyler Lowrey, and Bill Stover have resigned as directors.
Micron said Stover will continue to serve as chief financial officer and vice president for finance, and Heitzeberg will remain vice president for design, product engineering and quality assurance.
Lowrey, formerly chief operations officer, will now be responsible for research and development of advanced technology.
The company did not say if Lowrey's previous position will be filled with another executive.
Micron said the board intends to evaluate adding additional independent directors "who can bring added outside industry expertise and experience to the company."

"These changes will provide for a more independent board and will give the directors an opportunity to evaluate additional members who will bring new strength to our board," said Steve Appleton, Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer.
Micron manufacturers semiconductors and memory chips. In the year ended August 29, the company reported a profit of $593.5 million, down from $844.1 million the year earlier.
